The Cognitive Reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ;  Gross and John, 2003 )

The Cognitive Reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ;  Gross and John, 2003 ), translated into Chinese ( Shi, 2012 ), was used to measure individual differences in habitual cognitive reappraisal.

description.value: The six-item Cognitive Reappraisal subscale of the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire, translated into Chinese, measured individual differences in habitual cognitive reappraisal. It was administered to characterize participants and assess baseline group equivalence; Cronbach's alpha was 0.80.

spans.text: The scale consists of six items. Participants rated statements on a 7-point scale from 1 (strongly disagree) to 7 (strongly agree) to indicate how much the items were representative of their behavior. The scale had an acceptable Cronbach’s alpha of 0.80 in the present study.
The Positive and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS;  Watson et al., 1988 )
The Positive and Negative Affect Scale (PANAS;  Watson et al., 1988 ), translated into Chinese ( Huang et al., 2003 ), was used to measure participants’ affective state in the preceding week.

description.value: The 20-item Positive and Negative Affect Scale, translated into Chinese, measured positive and negative affect during the preceding week. It was administered to characterize participants and assess baseline group equivalence; Cronbach's alpha was 0.88 for positive affect and 0.89 for negative affect.

spans.text: On the second level, we estimated a flexible factorial design with three factors (subject, instruction type, and provocative condition) in the decision phase.
